review_text: I play a lot of casual puzzle games and normally I stop playing somewhere between level 50 and level 200 and certainly by level 450. They get boring or they get greedy and try to make things so hard that you must use boosters that you must purchase with real money. Smash Fest has stayed interesting challenging at a pleasant level and since it basically does not use boosters has not forced me into buying them. I am currently at level 2221 and expect I’ll keep going for the foreseeable future. I have played several other highly similar games and Smash Fest has the most satisfying physics of any that I have played and has a more pleasant soundscape several similar games do you break the glass bottles? Have such high pitches that it is painful to listen to them smash vests are just fun so if you were looking for a game like this I strongly recommend it beyond the others.

review_title: Could be amazing but too greedy
review_text: Short version-Don’t do it!  For info I am just over level 1200-so I definitely have experience and have given it more than a reasonable chance. First the positive.  This game has the best graphics and smoothest action of all the bottle sort games I have tried.  That is why I have stayed so long.  It has the potential to be the best, most relaxing of it’s kind. But unfortunately that is where the fun ends.  It is just an exceptionally greedy money grab with a game sometimes.  Win a round, watch an ad.  Lose a round, watch an ad. Want more time, watch an ad.  And the ads are repetitive, annoying, aggressive, offensive, difficult to opt out, and some are not even remotely correctly targeted.  I will NEVER EVER download Royal Match or Gossip Harbor-I would rather play with 2 broken sticks in an icy mud puddle during a lightning storm!  Most of the gambling and crypto apps will not let you just simply move on, you are forced to go to the app store and then navigate back to the game. Some have shown sexually suggestive images.  Some ask you if you are interested and even if you say no they are right back again soon as if they never asked.  I am definitely not the target demographic for many ads that are forced down my throat.  And on and on and on.  Then the game itself.  Exceptionally challenging is too generous.  It’s rigged and downright mean.  It’s hard to earn coins in any amount to be useful. Many times you can get stuck in the first few moves after turning over colors you can’t see.  Once you get stuck you instantly lose-no backing up, no using an extra bottle you already have-the only way to continue is to spend coins.  If you do buy a bottle and still turn over the wrong color-sudden death and that bottle is gone.  Other versions of this app allow you to keep the extra bottle until that level is complete.  Sometimes you spend your hard-earned coins to sort a bottle.  More than once I have paid to sort just 2 colors and it put them back exactly how they were.  Coins lost, sudden death, game over, try again-watch this ad. There are some levels that are impossible.  I have had times where I got free minutes and played 50+  tries and still not made it.  Then magically after a day or so being stuck, it decides you are worthy and permits you to complete the level.  Twice I have been so frustrated that I paid the $2 ransom for another bottle.  The last 20 or so rounds have been win one easy, then endless tries to win one, repeat cycle.  If you are graced with extra time you have to use it immediately-(what if I have something else to do?)-there is no way to save it or even give it away in one of the bajillion sub-games that make no sense.  What would I like to see?  A bought version with no ads.  No sub-games or maybe one.  Allow me to start over and replay a level if I get stuck.  Allow me to back up when stuck without sudden death.  I would watch an ad for an extra bottle.  I want to have fun and try different sequences of filling bottles.  This one is no fun anymore.    If you love watching endless repetitive ads or just paying through the nose for more bottles, then this one is for you.  If life is too short for repetitive ads, try a different app.  An app is supposed to make things better-I just stay frustrated with it continually.  I earned a bottle at 1200.  Once it’s gone, I’m done with this game.

I’m learning how it’s done…then-here we go! You absolutely can’t finish levels with what they give you, so you either can’t play for awhile(and i believe most people play when they have a few minutes, not waiting until you build up lives) or you HAVE to buy coins to get the extra milk bottles. I’ve had so many games where IMMEDIATELY yiu have to try again and/or buy another milk bottle and you do  and the VERY next move, you have no moves and need another milk bottle! 😡 That’s 2800 to play that one level! So, you literally cannot play this game without purchasing their coins. The further up in levels you go, the more that happens. So, uninstalling and hopefully you can find a better game than this one. It stinks.

review_title: From Strategy Game to Whale Game — Even $1,000/Month Isn’t Enough
review_text:
I’ve played Whiteout Survival for about a year and have genuinely enjoyed the game. In the beginning, it felt like a strategy game: build your city, develop your heroes, join an alliance, work together, plan rallies, and compete against other alliances in Castle Battle, State vs. State, and other events.

Unfortunately, the game I enjoyed is increasingly disappearing.

Whiteout Survival has become dominated by an escalating pay-to-compete model where a handful of extremely high-spending “whales” can determine the outcome of major events. Strategy and alliance coordination still matter, but increasingly the strategy becomes: “How do we deal with their whale?”

I’m not writing this as a free-to-play player upset that paying players have an advantage. I’m a mid-level spender who has spent as much as $1,000 per month on this game. I used to be competitive enough to lead rallies. Today, spending roughly the same amount, I’ve effectively become a rally joiner because I cannot keep pace with the constant introduction of new power systems, upgrades, heroes, gear, and other paid progression.

Think about that before downloading: $1,000 per month can still leave you feeling underpowered.

The biggest problem is that there is no realistic point where you “catch up.” Every time players make progress, another system or progression layer raises the ceiling. Someone willing to spend thousands more can simply buy an enormous power advantage. That makes previous investments feel increasingly obsolete.

And that changes the psychology of the game. Instead of thinking, What strategy should our alliance use?, you increasingly think, How much more would I have to spend to remain relevant?

I understand that mobile games need to make money, and I have willingly supported this one financially. But there is a difference between paying to progress faster and creating an ecosystem where competitive relevance increasingly requires unlimited spending.

My advice to new players: be very cautious before spending money on Whiteout Survival. The early game is fun and can make relatively modest purchases feel valuable. But the further you progress, the more expensive maintaining that competitive position becomes.

I would gladly continue supporting this game if the developers restored more value to strategy, alliance coordination, and long-term progression and reduced the enormous competitive gap created by unlimited spending.

Until then, I cannot recommend investing significant money into this game. There is always another whale, another upgrade, and another finish line.

The matchmaking continues to create frustrating experiences. New servers and older servers often end up with wildly different spending levels, making many competitive events feel decided by wallets instead of strategy. Rather than balancing gameplay, the developers continue introducing more power creep that only widens the gap.

The amount of pop ups, advertisements, limited time offers, battle passes, and daily purchase prompts has become ridiculous. Logging in doesn’t feel like opening a strategy game anymore. It feels like opening a storefront that occasionally lets you play.

The worst part is watching players quit. I’ve seen alliances fall apart, entire states die, whales stop spending, long time leaders retire, and friends leave because they’re simply tired of chasing the next expensive update. When even the people spending thousands of dollars are saying enough is enough, that should be setting off alarms. Instead, the developers just release another pack.

What makes all of this even more frustrating is that none of it feels accidental anymore. It feels deliberate. Every decision appears focused on maximizing revenue instead of building a game people actually want to play for years to come.

After more than 3 years, I honestly can’t recommend Whiteout Survival to anyone. Not because the core gameplay is terrible, but because the people running it have made it painfully clear that profit comes before players every single time.

If you’re thinking about starting this game, understand what you’re getting into. You’re not joining a strategy game that’s growing with its community. You’re joining a game that has become another cash grab, where transparency doesn’t exist, customer support is useless, player feedback is ignored, and every update asks one question:

“How much more money can we get from our players before they finally walk away?”

The developers need to understand the concept of updates timed with server progression. For the first year or so upgrades came along with new generations. Now they just slam upgrades down and apply to all without allowing players to plan out upgrades or gather materials. The greed is sickening. What use to be a game I could keep up with on a modest budget has lost all appeal. If you’re still playing this in 2026, what are you doing.

review_title: Aggressive monetization, moving goalposts, and meaningless support
review_text:
I’ve invested significant time and money into Whiteout Survival, but the game has become increasingly difficult to recommend.

The developers repeatedly raise the progression ceiling before players and states have a reasonable opportunity to catch up. New upgrades are introduced in ways that create constant spending pressure, while competitive power becomes more concentrated among a small number of extremely high-spending players. Strategy, coordination, and long-term progression matter less every time another expensive system is added.

What makes this worse is the customer-service experience. When I raised detailed concerns about competitive balance, player retention, and the escalating cost of remaining competitive, I received a generic response saying my feedback would be “documented.” There was no meaningful engagement, no follow-up, and no indication that the underlying issue was taken seriously.

Quality-of-life improvements and overdue gameplay features are welcome, but they do not offset a monetization model that continually moves the finish line. Long-term customers should feel valued, not demoralized and pressured to spend thousands more simply to maintain progress they already paid heavily to achieve.

Until the developers slow the progression treadmill, improve competitive balance, and demonstrate that player feedback leads to real action, I cannot recommend this game.

review_title: Spent Money on an Event That Is Broken — Support Hasn’t Fixed It
review_text:
I’m extremely frustrated with Board Adventure right now. I spent real money specifically to participate in the Merge Heaven event, progressed all the way to the point where my board should reset so I can continue to the next stage, and it simply does not work.

Other members of my clan have been able to progress normally, so this clearly isn’t how the event is supposed to work. I’ve tried everything I can on my end, including clearing the board and leaving only the crowned/max-level piece, but the game will not advance.

I already contacted support about the problem. I received an email and an in-game gift as if the issue had been addressed, but the actual problem was never fixed. Even more frustrating, I can’t reply to that email, and the in-game support option just redirects me to a website where I haven’t been able to actually get help.

I wouldn’t be nearly as upset if this were just a free event, but I spent money specifically on this event and now I’m unable to use what I paid for because of a bug. At this point, I either want the event fixed while I still have an opportunity to complete it or I want the money I spent on it refunded.

I enjoy the game, but taking purchases for a limited-time event and then leaving a player unable to progress because of a bug—with no effective way to reach support—is incredibly disappointing. I’ll gladly update this review if the issue is actually resolved.

And if you are just looking for a lobby to join all you had to do was just looking for the map you wanted and click play, once you join you just pick the color you wanted and accessories. This is a terrible game for anyone who just wants to play casually.

I actually kept track of around 80 battles. Only 3 out of those 80 matched me against someone even remotely close to my level. The rest were mostly level 100 players, fully upgraded castles, or teams filled with premium characters. You can regularly get matched against someone who has clearly spent a lot more money and has a massive advantage before the battle even starts.

And then there’s the laser controlled character. Everyone already knows how ridiculously strong this character is, which is exactly why you see people using it constantly. In 3–4 turns it can basically wipe out your entire team. Somehow it also seems to consistently attack the exact position you just fired from. There is very little strategy involved when one character gives such a huge advantage.

At first I thought this was going to be a great game because it reminded me of Worms. Unfortunately, after playing for a while, it mostly gives you stress and frustration instead of fun.

I don’t see the point of spending around $40 just to level the playing field against the opponents the matchmaking system keeps giving you.

From a business perspective, the developers did a great job creating reasons for players to spend money. From a gameplay and balance perspective, there isn’t much positive I can say.

review_title: Fun at first but quickly becomes pay to play
review_text:
I genuinely enjoyed this game when I first started playing, but after a few days the problems became impossible to ignore. For a game that is supposed to be about fashion and styling, it feels less like creativity matters and more like how much you’re willing to spend.

Many of the better clothing, makeup, hair, and accessory options require premium currency, and that currency disappears FAST. If you actually want enough options to style outfits properly or have a realistic chance in the competitions, the game constantly pushes you toward spending real money.

The competitions also feel incredibly inconsistent and honestly rigged. You can put together an outfit that actually follows the challenge theme and still rank extremely low, while outfits that barely seem related to the prompt rank significantly higher. That makes the entire competition system feel pointless. If following the prompt and creating a coordinated outfit doesn’t matter, what exactly are we being judged on?

And the POP-UPS. There are way too many. The game constantly wants you to buy something, subscribe to something, sign up for something, claim some offer, or spend premium currency. I want to play a fashion game, not repeatedly close advertisements and purchase prompts just to get back to the actual game.

There’s a genuinely fun fashion game underneath all of this, which makes it even more frustrating. Give players reasonable ways to earn premium currency, make competitions feel fair and actually based on the stated themes, provide enough free styling options to remain creative, and seriously reduce the constant monetization pop-ups.

I shouldn’t have to open my wallet every five minutes just to enjoy a dress-up game. 🤮

review_text: Paper.io 2 is an absolute, unmitigated technical disaster, a flagrant piece of deceptive engineering, a predatory corporate vehicle, and a psychological exercise in player exploitation that easily ranks as one of the most insulting, dishonest, and fundamentally broken titles ever permitted onto the App Store. What purports to be a smooth, casual, competitive multiplayer expansion of a classic area-conquering arcade concept is, in truth, a hollow simulation meticulously engineered from the ground up to harvest user data, drain device batteries, and force-feed an unrelenting barrage of unskippable advertisements to a hostage audience. The most egregious and unforgivable deception lies in the game’s core marketing premise: the illusion of a global, real-time multiplayer arena. You are never, under any circumstances, playing against actual human beings; instead, you are dropped into a localized ghost theater populated entirely by synthetic, algorithmically driven artificial intelligence bots disguised with random, stolen human usernames and arbitrary country flags. These bots do not operate on human latency, organic spatial awareness, or realistic tactical decision-making; they are programmed as omniscient, heat-seeking missiles designed to track your coordinates perfectly across the map and execute frame-accurate strikes on your exposed tail the exact millisecond your colored territory reaches a substantial or meaningful percentage of the board. This creates a deeply synthetic, artificial, and inherently rigged difficulty curve where your strategic movements, fast reflexes, and spatial planning are completely irrelevant, as the underlying code will actively spawn an enemy bot directly outside your immediate rendering viewpoint, moving at speeds that defy the game’s physics, just to clip your tail line and force a game-over screen. This rigged loop is not a byproduct of poor programming, but a deliberate, calculated mechanism designed to maximize player turnover and drive you directly into the game’s primary function: an aggressive, predatory ad-delivery engine. The sheer frequency, duration, and obnoxiveness of the advertisements in Paper.io 2 border on psychological warfare, with a mandatory, non-skippable 30-to-60-second video ad triggering instantly after every single round you play. Given that the hyper-aggressive AI bots ensure the average organic round lasts less than ten to fifteen seconds, you routinely spend vastly more time locked in an unskippable marketing loop than you do interacting with the actual game interface. To compound this insult, these ads are intentionally designed with highly deceptive, microscopic 'X' buttons, fake interactive countdown timers, and delayed close graphics that intentionally hijack your finger taps, redirecting your device away from the game and forcing open the external App Store to artificially boost click-through rates. The game offers a 'revive' feature to save your high score, but this is merely another trap to extort another 30 seconds of your life for a corporate video impression, only for the game to respawn your avatar directly into the mouth of another bot, killing you instantly a second time. Even during the brief moments of active gameplay, the screen is cluttered with flickering, high-contrast banner ads at the bottom of the user interface that constantly refresh, putting immense strain on the rendering engine and inducing severe frame-rate drops, stuttering, and catastrophic input lag. From a technical performance standpoint, Paper.io 2 is a total trainwreck that lacks even a basic understanding of hardware optimization, turning high-end iOS smartphones into literal, overheating bricks within five to ten minutes of launching the application. The battery drain is nothing short of catastrophic, devouring multiple percentage points of battery life per minute as the unoptimized code causes the internal processors to run at maximum thermal capacity, which triggers aggressive system-level thermal throttling. Once thermal throttling initiates, the game's input responsiveness drops off a cliff; your subtle directional swipes are completely dropped by the engine, causing your avatar to travel stubbornly in a straight line, completely ignoring your frantic commands to curve back to safety, leaving your tail permanently exposed until an AI bot inevitably destroys you. This technical failure is mirrored in the absolute broken state of the game's collision-detection algorithms and physics engine, which are riddled with game-breaking bugs and erratic clipping issues. You will routinely witness enemy bots glide effortlessly right through your solid, fully captured, locked-in territory lines without suffering any penalty or dying, yet if your own character model so much as grazes its own trail due to a micro-stutter or a visual mismatch on the screen, the game instantly registers an error and obliterates your progress. The visual boundary lines are completely inconsistent, meaning you are never truly safe even deep within your own color grid, as the game frequently registers abstract deaths with zero visual indicators or logical explanations. Furthermore, the progression, unlocking, and customization systems are entirely superficial and broken, promising an array of vibrant skins, unique avatars, and environmental textures for achieving specific operational milestones, such as conquering 50%, 80%, or 100% of the arena map. However, the game's internal data-tracking and cloud-saving architecture are fundamentally broken; you can spend hours battling the rigged AI to finally cross a threshold, unlock a coveted skin, and close the app, only to find the app has completely wiped your local cache upon the next boot, locking the skin away once more and forcing you to repeat the miserable process. There is a complete lack of structural integrity, a total absence of respect for the user's time, and zero regard for the preservation of player data or achievements

Candy Crush Saga isn’t a puzzle game. It’s a monetization engine disguised as one.

Almost every aspect of the game feels carefully designed to push you into spending money. The visuals, sounds, constant pop-ups, limited-time offers, races against other players, and endless prompts to buy boosters all create pressure to pay rather than simply enjoy playing.

Some levels don’t feel challenging because of skill. They feel deliberately designed to make you run out of moves so you’re tempted to buy extra ones or purchase boosters. It’s incredibly frustrating when success seems to depend more on your wallet than your ability.

The timed competitions are another example. They encourage players to spend money just to keep up, turning what should be a casual game into a race driven by purchases rather than enjoyment.

My biggest concern is how this affects younger or more vulnerable players. The game is full of psychological nudges that encourage spending, and I would strongly advise parents not to let children play it if they have access to payment methods.

There are plenty of genuinely enjoyable puzzle games that reward strategy and skill. In my opinion, this isn’t one of them. It feels designed first and foremost to maximize spending.

I have played more than 12,000 levels of this game, and for a long time I genuinely enjoyed it. Unfortunately, that is no longer the case.
The game increasingly feels designed to make players fail unless they spend money on extra moves. Instead of rewarding skill and strategy, many levels seem intentionally unbalanced to encourage in-app purchases.
The developers have also introduced new features, such as card collections, but those are equally frustrating. Completing collections requires rare gold cards that cannot be traded with teammates, making it extremely difficult—if not impossible—to finish without relying on luck or spending money.
To make matters worse, the rewards for completing events and challenges are underwhelming and rarely justify the amount of time and effort required. Overall, what was once an enjoyable and engaging game now feels more focused on monetization than on providing a fair and rewarding experience for its players.

I’ve also seen server leaders and high-ranking players engage in bullying, targeting, and toxic behavior toward other players, which creates a hostile environment. While not every server is the same, these issues have been common enough that I would not feel comfortable allowing a child to play.

If you’re an adult, you may enjoy the strategy, events, and alliance aspects of the game as I have. But if you’re a parent looking for a game for your child, I would recommend waiting until they’re at least 18 years old or ensuring you can closely monitor their interactions.

The game itself is decently fun. I will warn you not to spend any money though. The item will promise items and you may or may not receive it. Good game. Not much like the adds to get you to download.  On top of that, once you play for a bit, the adds become overwhelming. Sad they ruin a good game with adds and lies.

The forced ads after a certain level of progression make this game dang near unplayable. 

FYI it’s $7.99 to remove ONLY the mandatory ads. The other ads still remain. 

Game is fun, progression is fun, characters and weapon designs are fun. The paywall is a major downer.

Ads

Chapter 1 is a masterclass on getting users to watch ads. Every ad provided real value and seriously accelerated progression. I treated the ads like mini games and blew through the first 100 levels easily. The game itself didn’t get that much play time as the ads contributed significantly. 

Chapter 2 was the same as chapter 1 but ads were no longer the only driving force. You got to choose which ads to watch because the value proposition dropped significantly.

Chapter 3 is entirely about game play. The value of the ads tanked and they’re only worth doing to complete the daily quests.

Gameplay
Chapters can be traversed and there is real value in going back to old chapters to quickly get items. The progression is exponential so after you get into chapter 2 you can go back to chapter 1 and have no fear of possibly dying.

Progression is super fast in chapter 1, only took me 3 days. Chapter 2 took 5 days. I can already tell that chapter 3 will take weeks.

The core loop of the game is best seen when you go to previous chapters. Run around the arena to kill monsters and get items. Collect all the chests and come back to them when the timer is up. After this core loop, you use the items collected to complete daily tasks like making weapons. There are some mini games like the challenge tower, boss raids, and invasions. None of the mini games are very valuable individually but combined with the events they are worth doing. The mini games are mostly deterministic at the start but later on there is some variety. For example, I can easily finish the second raid boss on expert mode but the first mini boss which has fewer requirements is basically impossible because the boss shield absorbs 300 hits regardless of how much damage they hit for. 

You have to finish the quest requirements in order to move on to the next chapter. This is a pain point because you can easily beat the chapter boss at 20 below and there is a slow tedious grind to level up. I am at level 204 right now and it feels like it would take several hours of auto play to get to 205. For the game to introduce itself as constant progression and a source of dopamine and then halt progression feels a bit icky. 

Purchases
I’ve bought the skip ads pack which claimed to remove all forced ads. It does help a lot but there have been a few times I left my phone to auto battle and came back to ad. The 5 ad skips a day are great but become less valuable as you progress through the game.

I also purchased the event pass for the new hero. I got kinda stuck where it would have taken me much longer to finish chapter 2 and I knew that the new hero would make it easier. Unfortunately, even though the purchase said guaranteed hero it didn’t just give me the hero outright, I still had to earn it which took a couple days. I would have preferred the purchase instantly gave me the materials required to unlock the hero and then any future materials could have been used to level it up. As it stands, the hero I purchased could have been earned normally and the price I paid for what I got doesn’t feel worth it. After this event, I don’t know how else I will get the materials required to level the hero up, which caps how strong it can get.

Lastly, everything you can purchase helps to a degree but there’s nothing that feels like purchasing it would get you past the next hard grind. I know this is pay to win I’m asking for but I’d rather get to the end game quickly and keep grinding in preparation for chapter 4 than to actively slog through.

Final thoughts
I really enjoyed the last week playing this game but I don’t plan to make any more purchases or watch a ton of ads. They simply aren’t rewarding enough at this stage. I’ll try the daily grind for an hour a day and see where that takes me. Overall, it’s certainly worth playing.

EDIT: After another week I went from 200 to 213 and I’m uninstalling. Even if I pay $100 I doubt it would get me through chapter 3. The progression is so bloody slow now I wish I uninstalled the game last week. 21 hours later and even more auto hunting and I am still exactly where I was last week. At 204 I could beat up to 250 bosses and that remains true at 213. To make matters worse, the invasion mini game is no longer just a time sink, it’s a time sink for even less rewards. The rewards that are given out after doing every daily challenge to the max and watching all the ads to get as much as possible is barely moving the needle. At this point my previous experience has been completely shadowed by an obvious money hungry paywall. It wasn’t worth noting before because auto hunting wasn’t really needed that much but the game is very demanding and absolutely drains the battery. Download the game, beat the first two chapters and don’t look back. I really wanted to see the other areas because this game’s art style and enemy variety is pretty neat but it’s not worth spending thousands to do so. Genuinely, if they let me get to end game and grind for the 4th chapter I would have spent way more money on this game but with this exponential requirement increase I’m not having fun anymore and there’s no point.

I wrote like 20 paragraphs but forgot the save the draft… I’ll be quick this time, promise. I had low expectations going in, so very little was surprising. The games loop was fun enough that I held my tongue even if it got a bit annoying. However the new update is the last straw for me, quite a few gems I’ve collected over time got wiped away in the update. Along with my patience for the ads finally running thin. Every 3 minutes or so I’m forced to watch an ad, which seems a bit too common but whatever. And even if they didn’t have ads, they made sure to have optional pop ups as well. Money, auto clicker, etc, the entire game feels like a giant cash grab… Also the grinders taking time has ruined my experience. It seems like such a trivial thing to change however its reinvigorated my hatred for the game as a whole. I’ve personally sat around for 15 minutes watching the grinder struggle to deal with the pileup of coins at its base. So now not only do I have to sit around twiddling my thumbs while I wait for the grinder to do its job, I also get the wonderful taste of ads every few minutes inconveniencing me further. I truly believe developers, especially indie ones, deserve to make money from their creations. After all they put hard work into creating them. HOWEVER the industry as a whole and this game especially is taking advantage of people. The entire point of making a game is because you have an idea you love and want to make it a reality. Maybe even get others to love your work too. All people do now if try to suck every last penny out of their games as they can. Which has drained my enjoyment for games in their entirety. It’s a scummy thing to do just for a few extra Pennie’s, and developers need to dial it back.

All in all, could be a good game but it’s got some fixes that it needs.

review_title: Greed has taken over this once awesome game.
review_text:
I’ve played Gardenscapes on and off for years, and it’s disappointing to see what this game has become. It used to be fun because there was a good balance of easy, medium, and hard levels. Some levels challenged you, some were relaxing, but overall it felt fair. You could actually make progress without feeling like you had to spend money.

Once you get past level 11,000, that balance is gone. Almost every level feels like a Hard or Super Hard level, even the ones that aren’t labeled that way. The difficulty feels intentionally increased to push players toward buying coins, boosters, and extra moves.

The coin rewards are also terrible. You can spend multiple lives and boosters trying to beat a difficult level, only to get rewarded with a small amount of coins that doesn’t come close to replacing what you used. The payout system makes progression feel like a constant struggle.

Gardenscapes has gone from a fun puzzle game to a pay-to-win cash grab. Instead of rewarding the players who have stuck with this game for years, the developers have made it more and more frustrating unless you’re willing to spend money.

It’s disappointing because this used to be one of my favorite games. After years of playing, I find myself enjoying it less and less because the focus seems to have shifted from creating a fun experience to finding more ways to get players to pay. Unless you’re willing to spend money, expect more frustration than fun.

review_title: Auto Play AI Needs Smarter Decision Making
review_text:
I really enjoy playing eFootball, and I appreciate the effort the developers put into the game. However, I would like to suggest an improvement to the AI in Auto Play Mode, especially in eFootball League.

The opponent’s AI plays intelligently, makes good decisions, creates realistic attacking moves, and defends well. On the other hand, my team’s AI often makes poor decisions, inaccurate passes, predictable runs, and unnecessary mistakes, regardless of how highly rated my players are. It feels like my team’s AI does not perform according to the players’ abilities and ratings.

I have a finger injury from an accident, so I cannot play using manual controls. Auto Play Mode is the only way I can enjoy the game. I have spent time building my dream team, choosing the right formations, making substitutions, and adjusting attacking and defensive tactics. It would be great if the AI controlling my team could make smarter decisions and provide a more realistic football experience.

Please improve the Auto Play AI so that it is more intelligent, less predictable, and better reflects each player’s attributes and ratings. This would make Auto Play Mode more enjoyable and fair for players like me who rely on it.

Thank you for creating such a great football game. I hope you will consider improving this feature in future updates.

# Why Ninja Kiwi Made the Best Game Ever and Why BTD6 Needs a Banana Farm Paragon

When it comes to tower defense games, **Bloons TD 6 (BTD6)** by Ninja Kiwi stands above the rest. Since its release, the game has continued to grow with frequent updates, new towers, heroes, maps, and game modes that keep players coming back. Its combination of strategy, replayability, and fun has made it one of the greatest tower defense games ever created.

One of the biggest reasons BTD6 is so successful is Ninja Kiwi's dedication to the community. Instead of releasing the game and moving on, the developers regularly add new content, balance towers, fix bugs, and listen to player feedback. This level of support has helped BTD6 stay fresh for years and has built a loyal fan base.

The gameplay itself is another reason why BTD6 is so enjoyable. Players must carefully choose which towers to place, upgrade them wisely, and adapt to increasingly difficult waves of bloons. The addition of Heroes, Paragons, Boss Bloons, and co-op mode gives players countless ways to experience the game. Whether someone is a beginner or an expert trying to beat the hardest challenges, there is always something new to learn.

One feature that many players would love to see is a **Banana Farm Paragon**. Banana Farms are one of the most important support towers in the game because they generate money, allowing players to afford stronger defenses. A Banana Farm Paragon could become the ultimate economy tower by combining the strengths of all three upgrade paths. It could produce enormous amounts of cash, automatically collect bananas, generate lives like the Monkey Wall Street, and perhaps even provide buffs to nearby Banana Farms. To keep it balanced, it could also have an extremely high cost so that players would need to invest heavily before unlocking its full power.

Adding a Banana Farm Paragon would give players another exciting late-game goal and complete the lineup of powerful Paragon towers. It would also encourage creative strategies focused on maximizing income before unleashing the strongest defenses possible.

In conclusion, Ninja Kiwi has made one of the best games ever with Bloons TD 6 by consistently supporting it with high-quality updates and engaging gameplay. While the game already offers an incredible experience, adding a Banana Farm Paragon would be an exciting addition that many fans would enjoy. If Ninja Kiwi continues to expand BTD6 with creative ideas like this, the game will remain one of the greatest tower defense games for years to come.

review_title: Good Fun but Room or Improvement
review_text:
Graphics are impressive, and I like that you can choose at which level (easy, medium, hard) individual opponents play.

Unfortunately the game can be a little busy. Before each player's roll, a banner pops up announcing the turn. Then the focus zooms in on their piece as it moves around the board. All of this makes it difficult to take in the property situation on the board. 

A bigger problem is that all property of a bankrupt player goes to the player who bankrupted them. There is no option to return the assets to the bank. This almost always means the bankrupted will win in short order. What's frustrating is there is an option to have the game end in that scenario, with the player who caused their opponent to go bankrupt being the winner. The game would benefit from also having the option to return forefieted property returned to the pot.

Pros and cons of FNAF:
Pros:
1. Cheap. Only $2.99.
2. Fun! Great if you like being scared.
3. Not as scary as, say, The Exorcist.
Cons:
1. Jump scares. Little kids should not play this, even if they really want to.
2. Kinda boring until the animatronics move fast.
3. Challenging.

My age recommendation: 11+

Tips:
Conserve power!
Bonnie moves first.
Freddy doesn’t move until night three
If golden Freddy appears in your office and kills you, take a screenshot. That’s really rare. To avoid his jump scare, flip up the cameras immediately.
If you hear pots banging, it’s Chica in the kitchen. The camera there is disabled, but the audio still works.

review_title: Good game, too short for the price
review_text: I had a lot of fun playing this game and honestly think it was well developed and a unique idea, not to mention it has no ads. I understand that part of having no ads is the price point ($6.99 when I purchased) but I found that the amount of content you receive does not equate to the price point. In the game you only go through 4 “catalogs” of scratch cards with 4 different cards in them each, for a total of 16 cards and one final card (the prestige/death system). The game allows you to manually prestige but it’s better to just die and collect prestige points that way. All in all it took about 4 total prestiges/death to beat the game. There are various upgrades that you earn throughout the gameplay which are well designed and achievements as well that provide tickets for cosmetic upgrades. I was able to collect about 2/3 of the achievements on my first play through and due to future achievements only unlocking more cosmetic upgrades I didn’t really have a desire to play another life. Again I like the game a lot, but I think if you compare it to similar idle style games the mechanics are similar enough with much more content but many more ads.

review_text: I love this game on my PlayStation but it’s really frustrating to play on my phone. Even using a 17 Pro Max, which has a larger screen, it’s just super finicky. It’s annoying that since you’re swiping cards up from the bottom which frequently causes the phone go into app switcher, but it’s infuriating that frequently you accidentally play the wrong card or use a potion on the wrong enemy, etc. The amount of runs I lost in only my first few tries because of discarding the wrong card or choosing the wrong card to return to my discard pile is outrageous. Besides all that, the UI isn’t scaled up, so all of the text is small and hard to read. Maybe it’s okay on an iPad, but it really needs to be rebuilt with a mobile focus for phones to justify a purchase.

review_title: Why do people say this game sucks its literally awesome
review_text: I love FNAF 2 more than any other game in the franchise which is why I was very surprised when I saw tons of my favorite Youtubers say it was the weakest when it came to gameplay.  This game while being very very chaotic is I think in one of its primes for the gameplay. In my opinion I think the music box mechanic is really really good. People say it makes the cameras completely useless because that’s the only camera you’ll ever be on, but if there wasn’t a music box, the cameras would just be completely useless. It’s a good, simple settlement management game, but unfortunately the base game lacks a proper endgame.

You can finish the entire campaign on the highest difficulty and even unlock Endless Mode, but it doesn’t really give you anything to do. You’ll quickly research every technology, clear the entire map, and that’s it. There are no new rewards for completing runs, no random maps, and no meaningful progression afterward.

Yes, you can reshuffle your unlocked perk deck and try different bonuses, but what’s the point if you’re just replaying the exact same content? The maps don’t become more challenging, and different leaders don’t significantly change the gameplay—they mostly provide a bonus and a drawback, while the core experience stays the same.

Overall, it’s an enjoyable game with a solid foundation, but without the DLC there’s only enough content for a few hours. Once you’ve finished the campaign, there’s simply nothing left to do.

I really hope the developers add a meaningful endgame to the base game, because the core gameplay is genuinely fun and deserves more replayability.

Absolutely fantastic game. This is easily one of the most addictive and cleverly designed roguelikes I’ve played on iOS. It scratches the same itch as Balatro and Luck Be a Landlord while still feeling completely original. There are so many interesting mechanics and interactions to discover that every run teaches you something new. I’ve already put a lot of hours into it, and I’m still finding new combinations and hidden systems.

My one request is for a higher animation speed—or even better, an option to skip the scoring animations entirely.

Once you get into the late game and builds are producing 40+ Ultra Jackpots or massive pattern chains every spin, the game becomes animation-bound rather than gameplay-bound. Even at 4× speed, a single spin can easily take over a minute to resolve. During your first successful run that’s exciting, but once you’ve already experienced it, those long waits become the biggest obstacle to replayability.

A 10× or 20× speed option, or a simple “Instant Resolve” / “Skip Scoring Animations” toggle, would make a huge difference for experienced players who want to keep pushing longer runs and experimenting with new builds without spending most of their time waiting for animations.

Other than that, this is an outstanding game and one of the best premium roguelikes available on iOS. Highly recommended.

review_title: Great Game but don't lock your phone mid-round.
review_text:
A great game like others have said, my only issue is I play at work or on the go and sometimes I have to step away mid-round. Especially in later deadlines when you have so many re-triggers and effects stacked upon one another. 

As long as the game stays running in the background everything is fine, but sometimes the game closes while my phone is locked, even when I don't touch it. 

The problem is the game really punishes you for closing it mid-round, I assume to prevent save-scumming. Not only do you lose the credits that you earned that round, but you also lose what you paid to start the round. This means if you did a full deposit before you will have 0 credits, basically forfeiting 2 rounds just because you locked your phone (or it locked itself). In later deadlines this is an instant game over and again, those are the rounds that this is most likely to happen. 

Now if it's due to device/engine limitations that sucks, and I hope some sort of middle of the road fix can be implemented. 

If it's done as an anti-save scum then it should be removed from the mobile version of the game in my opinion. Its just punishing everyone who plays the game on the go for how a handful of players choose to play the game. Players we don't know or  interact with in any way.

I really love this game, please fix these bugs and optimize the camera rendering in the next update. Thank you very much.

review_title: New features that should be added to the game
review_text:
I have an idea that could make the flight simulator feel even more like the real world.First, it would be amazing if the scenery included more detailed cities with realistic buildings, neighborhoods, roads, highways, moving cars, traffic lights, and people. Seeing a living world below the aircraft would make every flight feel much more immersive.
Another feature I’d love is the ability to leave the cockpit and walk around. Players could walk through the airport terminal, check in, go through security, wait at the gate, board the aircraft, and walk through the cabin before taking their seat in the cockpit. Being able to explore the inside of every aircraft would make the experience much more realistic.It would also be great to improve cabin realism by adding many more flight attendant voice announcements and allowing players to speak using a built-in pilot voice or microphone for ATC and passenger announcements.
Also The ground operations could also be expanded. Ground crew should walk around the aircraft performing inspections, loading baggage, connecting ground power, fueling the aircraft, guiding the plane with marshalling wands, removing wheel chocks, and communicating with the flight crew. Ground service vehicles such as fuel trucks, baggage carts, catering trucks, belt loaders, and pushback tugs should all move around the airport and perform their jobs automatically. Finally, airports could feel more alive by having passengers walking through terminals, boarding planes, airport employees working, service vehicles driving around, and aircraft arriving and departing throughout the day. These features would make the simulator feel like a true living aviation world rather than just a place to fly airplanes. I believe these additions would make the simulator one of the most realistic and immersive flight simulation experiences available.

I’ve been playing Real Flight Simulator for about 4–5 years, and overall I love the game. It’s one of the best mobile flight simulators out there, but there are a few major issues that have been frustrating me for a long time.

My biggest complaint is multiplayer. Players can taxi straight through or into your aircraft with no collision avoidance. It completely ruins the realism and immersion. This has been an issue for years, and I really think it should be addressed in a future update.

Another feature the game desperately needs is a fully functional AI ATC system with voice communication. Being able to talk to Ground, Tower, Departure, Approach, and Center would make the simulator feel far more realistic instead of relying on basic menus.

Emergency operations also need a major overhaul. If I declare an emergency, emergency vehicles should automatically respond and be waiting after I land. I shouldn’t have to press five or ten different buttons just to get emergency services. That takes away from the realism, especially during critical situations.

I’d also love to see many more aircraft failures added, such as:

* Cabin fires
* Cargo fires
* Smoke in the cockpit
* Electrical fires
* Hydraulic failures
* Fuel leaks
* Engine fires that spread
* Pressurization failures and other realistic emergency scenarios

I’ve supported this game for years because I genuinely enjoy it, but it feels like some of these important features have been ignored for too long. Instead of focusing mostly on new aircraft and airports, I hope the developers put more effort into realism, multiplayer improvements, and emergency systems. These changes would take an already great simulator to the next level.

This port of the original Papers, Please is a neatly constructed and well-made adaptation to mobile phones. Also there’s this small glitch that IF you want someone’s fingerprints or you wanna search them, if you tap too fast, for some reason it detains them. The route card draws don’t feel random (skewed in favor of AI players, and against me), AI players are able to collect the colors they need far faster and easier than I can, and here lately, AI players only seem interested in keeping 3-4 route cards while collecting as many colors as possible and dropping their trains all in rapid succession to score a ton of points. Can’t tell you how many times I’ve completed 8-9 routes, and still lost by 40 points to an AI player who completed 3, but racked up 95 points. Sure, it’s a strategy to win a game if you can collect a bunch of color cards, but it’s the virtual equivalent of losing a video game to a kid who does nothing but button mash. I’ve even tried to use this method against the AI, but it doesn’t work, because I can’t collect colors fast enough, and the routes I’m given are short ones worth very little points most of the time.

This app used to be a fun way to hone my skills against real life players, but it’s next to unplayable now.

review_title: Complete version killed the mobile game
review_text: I’ve been a big Animal Crossing fan since Game Cube days. I played the mobile version, I guess going on 6 years. While the new “Complete” version had some really cool changes initially, the overall game is dead for existing players. No online gameplay, no visiting friend’s campsites, no new events, very few opportunities to obtain essence, etc. I would’ve gladly kept paying the monthly subscription if it meant the game continued. Slapping “complete” on the game title truly reads, “lazy ending”. I’m sad to leave the game behind after the years and money spent on a once beautiful game. If y’all ever decided to continue the game, many players would gladly come back.

Animal Crossing Pocket Camp is everything you could want and more, here’s why… first off, regular animal crossing, the one you’d get on a console, well you’d have to have one to play it. With this, all you need is an iPad or a phone, which makes it overall way more accessible. Secondly, it’s such a relaxing gameplay experience, and there is SO much you can do, as you might have read in the description. You can dress your character, you can make friends with the animals, you can gather fruit and elements of nature, you can design your cabin and your campsite, buy, sell and collect loads of cute furniture. One of the great things about Animal Crossing is just that it’s relaxing and free. Like say in, some games there is a goal or objective, but in this game you’re free to just hang out and design things, like your outfit or your camper van. You can make friends with animals, give them snacks, and SOO much more, that if I were to list everything it would be a lot. My wife and I sat down expecting a fun little game and stood up as different people with questions about our bloodlines.

The atmosphere is immaculate. The sound design is doing things that should be reported. The artwork is so gorgeous and so deeply wrong that it felt rude to look at it without a reservation. The puzzles are smart without being cruel, the lore is rich and completely unhinged in the best way, and somehow you and your partner end up doing real teamwork over what is essentially a dead man’s cryptic to-do list.

If you have not played this, you are eating fast food while a Michelin-star kitchen is right next door. 5 stars. We’re already ordering dessert.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Minor animatronics, cut characters, or one-off designs could finally have a role, making the night feel crowded and overwhelming in a good way. review_title: Winona and Walter bugs, and no caves progression issues
review_text:
Hi, I’ve been playing for a few weeks now and I noticed a few bugs:

1) Winona’s inspectacles (an important skill tree item) wouldn’t generate cachboxes and would just point in a direction past the world border. 

2) Walter can’t use woby (an in game mount he has) to dash with mobile controls which makes parts of his skill tree useless. 

Lastly as for progression issues, while I understand and completely agree that certain devices can’t support hosting servers with caves enabled, because mobile doesn’t have consol commands, servers that don’t have caves can’t progress to the games final bosses (the celestial champion and ancient fuelweaver) and the people on those servers can’t unlock their alignment skills on their skill trees as a result. Also important quality of life items like tingle nodes and star caller staffs are effectively unattainable in no caves servers. If server hosts just had access to some console commands a lot of these progression issues could be fixed. Also joining other servers for skill tree boss progression is extremely unreliable as most servers don’t communicate in the same language and can be extremely laggy.

review_title: Issac on iOS Can be GOOD! But HOLY PLEASE FIX THE GAME
review_text:
I’ve been playing the binding of Issac since it released on iOS when there weren’t any DLC and only Rebirth was on it, and after they released the DLCS, I bought them immediately!

The last Update was to fix Forgotten Needing A trinket to change to the ghost, and fixing pocket actives and adding more controls to Tainted Characters.

This was Almost 3 YEARS AGO, and ever since then, there has been countless bugs, unusable items + Trinkets, Awful control changes for no reason, save file corruption and many MANY more.

Issue One / The controls:
The Controls are really awful, and are a major downgrade from the previous ones before the DLCS were buyable, Dropping Trinkets are on the bottom left of the screen, now this sounds fine… but the button is INVISIBLE, not to mention, if you even GRAZE the near the trinket button, you simply stop moving and stop in-place, this is ABSOLUTELY AWFUL to deal with, and requires an unnecessary odd finger placement just to avoid the trinket button, and that’s just one of the issues, due to the screen now being much smaller, the Moving controls on iPad are AWFUL, they block the screen, are annoying, can make it difficult to use them if you drag them too far away from the area, and are simply a nuisance, this was not an issue as they were completely stopped in place in the previous update, now they move all over the place for no reason whatsoever.

Issue Two / Items + Trinkets + Items being unusable:
Items like D-Infinity and Blood Bombs / Trinkets like RC Remote and blood clots / golden bombs at 0 Bombs, and many more are simply useless without a controller, blood bombs and golden bombs can’t be used at 0 bombs due to the fact that the bombs button disappears at 0 bombs, items like D-Infinity can’t be switched due to the fact there’s no button or action to switch them, and RC car and Blood clots can’t allow you to move them separately due to the fact the button doesn’t appear, these items and trinkets and pickups can’t not be used without the use of a controller, and without a controller these things become UTTERLY USELESS making them pointless deadweight, in the previous update, you could switch D-Infinity with the trinket button due to it acting like a Key, but now that it’s been fixed, you simply can NOT use D-infinity or other items like it.

Issue Three / Dailies being (Semi)unplayable:
The button to play dailies is completely grayed out, so how are you meant to unlock some of the Unlocks that requires you to play Dailies? Simple! Just turn off airplane mode / the Wifi, turn it back on, and then QUICKLY press the button as the WiFi comes back on before it grays out again, this will take MANY attempts to even be able to do so, this is MISERABLE to deal with, and without the knowledge of what you need to do to ungray the button, it practically makes the unlocks Unobtainable.

The Third and biggest issue / complete Save file reversals / deletion:
Thankfully I’ve never experienced this issue, but the fact that this can happen is really bad, it isn’t possible to copy a save file so when one of these do happen, it is simply impossible to do anything, this is not only really awful, but can also be extremely demotivating and can Ruin the game and any enjoyment of it.

Yes the binding of Isaac is a very well made and fairly polished game, and While I enjoy the binding of Issac, I simply do not recommend YOU get it on iOS, it simply has too many issues for it to be worth it, all I can hope is one day these issues can be fixed, but until then, NEVER PLAY THIS GAME IN IOS.

Cons:
- You cannot create your own character.
- You have to drag the cupcake underneath the decorations (sprinkles) and toppings instead of bringing the toppings to the cupcakes. This mechanism feels extremely awkward and confusing, especially compared to some other Papa’s games.
- You will almost NEVER do a “Perfect” job with putting the frosting on. I’m not sure why, but no matter what I cannot get it to that “Perfect” status. Just “Great” and “Good”.
- Some buttons are too close together. I find myself tapping the cupcakes which puts more toppings on instead of pressing the button to switch which cupcake you’re decorating since the bottom is so close. The “X” (cancel button) is too close to the button that controls how much batter goes in the cupcake liner so I find myself throwing away cupcakes on accident.
- Getting under 50% on the decorating portion of the customer’s rating is very common. Everything else can be 100% besides the decorating and I’m not sure why.
- The visual quality of the game on the phone is super poor. Looks like some bootleg version.
- If you want to buy and use the doorbell, you have to have your audio on but that means having the music play on repeat in the background which some dislike (as stated in a previous review).
- The flow isn’t as smooth as other games with how long it takes to use the confusing decorating mechanisms and what not.

Pros:
- The side games are fun (to win tip $ and items for the shop).
- Placing the liners in the pan is easy.
- Squeezing the correct amount of batter in the liners is easy (as long as you don’t hit the “X”/cancel button)
- The oven part is fine.

I love basically all Papa’s cooking games. They have become a core part of my personality. Papa’s Paleteria offers the same charm and feel as all others, but the newest features added (namely the food truck) along with the much smoother graphics and gameplay make this one of the best mobile cooking games on the market. That said, in the context of other Papa’s games, the Paleteria gets a bit lost in the sauce. I’ve noticed as the quality of the newest games increase, so too does the difficulty (especially my personal favorite, Papa’s Mocharia), with time management playing a big role in perfecting each order. In this game, however, there seems to be an abundance of time. Half of each game day is spent holding down the booster button. Because the game is so simple, it can be become really easy, really fast. Decreasing the amount of time between orders would greatly improve the experience, as instead of holding down a booster half the time, I could have more to do in a shorter amount of time—this keeps me interested! 

i realize i am above the age demographic for Papa’s cooking games now (I am a 19 year old college student), but all other Papa’s games have held my interest since elementary school. Paleteria would be no different as long as the pacing was tweaked. Thank you for taking the time to read this, and I hope this helpful in some way. 

TLDR: great game, pacing issues

review_title: Broken Gameplay in Arabic Version – Exploited and Unfair
review_text:
The Arabic version of this game has a serious gameplay issue that completely ruins the experience. Because Arabic contains many words and variations, players have found an easy exploit: they use the first letter of each word as a clue system. This basically bypasses the intended mechanics and turns the game into something unfair and uncompetitive.

What’s worse is that a large percentage of players rely on this method—sometimes right from the start, but often switching to it when they begin losing. This removes any sense of skill, strategy, or fun. Instead of clever wordplay, the game becomes about exploiting a loophole that the system doesn’t seem capable of detecting or preventing.

As a result, matches feel pointless, especially for players who want to play the game as intended. Until this issue is addressed—either by improving moderation, restricting certain clue patterns, or adapting the system for Arabic—the game will continue to feel broken in this language.

I hope the developers take this seriously, because in its current state, the Arabic version is not enjoyable to play.

review_text:
I love this game so much ever since the moment I downloaded it back in 2022.  I remember like it was yesterday when I beat the story to the game.  But that was last year.  This game is the first Papa’s game to have a food truck option and I played with it for hours and hours it was so much fun!  Now, for the theory I have. (SPOILER) When Bonnie and Yalanda escaped prison at the final cutscene, it kinda left off as a cliffhanger and potentially a teaser for an upcoming game. If I had to come with a name it would be “Papa Louie 4: When Chicken Attacks”.  It sounds awful now that I am saying it out loud, but it might just happen.  Sadly, after Adobe Flash has been discontinued in 2020, I am having sad second thoughts.  If there is any other software that can help with your amazing website, I would love to play a new Papa Louie game.  Games like Cactus McCoy and Jacksmith just to name a few are really fun and worth playing.  Well, that’s all I have to say pretty much.

I love you Tony and Matt at Flipline Studios, and tell Papa Louie that I give you guys a Jojo blue ribbon

Fine for scratching the Catan itch on-the-go or while passively watching something on TV. Seafarers and Cities & Knights are worthy expansions with various scenarios and maps to choose from. I will probably pay for and play all of them over time because the prices are reasonable and it helps pass the time; though, I do wish other expansions could be added (such as The Helpers).

However, the AI has something very much to be desired here. The “stats” don’t seem to carry over to the actual game at all; you will quickly learn which bots are jerks and which are trying to play the game, and it has nothing to do with the stats that the game touts as a feature. Furthermore, they appear to unfairly target the human player; not necessarily because they are human, but because the CPU knows what resources the human player has and what cards they have, and because victory point cards are counted automatically they target the human player even if the victory point total is supposed to be hidden from them. On the note of the CPU programming, it was abundantly clear to me right away that the AI never takes any risks, regardless of supposed “skill level” (again, an issue with the “stats” not being applied in any tangible way). At least the digital console version features CPUs that will take the occasional risks on some trades.

Bottom line: don’t expect this version of the game to meaningfully train you up on solid Catan play. It is simply too basic for that purpose. But if you want to play Catan to pass some time, it does, at least, provide you with an avenue to do so. Functional as it is, however, it’s hard to recommend it to anyone that loves Catan in any and all of its forms.

review_title: Great Vibe, But Lacks the Frontiers Challange
review_text:
As a Kingdom Rush Frontiers fan, I went into this game with high hopes, and while it delivers a visually stunning and fresh experience, the core gameplay left me disappointed. The maps, heroes, towers, and hidden Easter eggs are all fantastic and beautifully designed. The two hero mechanic is top notch. However, if you are looking for a true tactical challenge, you won't find it here. Even on Veteran mode using only the free heroes and towers, the main campaign stages are surprisingly easy; once you figure out a few key tower patterns, you can simply spam them to clear every wave without much effort.
Stages 14,15 and additional campaigns are the only ones with true challenge (took me a few restarts to beat). Yet, please keep the main campaign difficulty to difficult when it’s veteran.

review_title: Don’t bother, this is just greedy.
review_text:
So, I sometimes use the Apple game thing to “demo” games and the Apple game thing has it where the ‘premium’ heroes can be unlocked via just playing through the game, so I figured here I could do the same thing.

I bought the two dlc, and then noticed the game itself felt like a slog to play, I didn’t have much fun, and it half felt like with how often it was tossing the diamonds at me, the premium currency, that okay fine, it’s a game where I’m meant to grind. Kinda annoying that every time I go into the hero tab to upgrade I’m reminded of all the paid for heroes but it’s fine, I can unlock them by playing the game.

No. You can’t.

The premium heroes and towers are purely purchase, for the paid for version, while the arcade version you MUST beat the level that the hero is attributed to.

The game isn’t fun, and after paying over twenty six dollars for just the dlc and base game, the game then demands you cough up another FIFTY DOLLARS for the premium heroes and towers. And I was even wondering why the towers felt so weak, compared to the DLC towers, cause I beat the entire game just spamming the dragon brood tower, cause it had a map-wide kinda mortar attack and a stun.

And then it hit me that the reason why is cause it’s trying to make you get the premium stuff, to pay that extra 50 (cause buying the towers/heroes solo would be a bit of a waste when the bundles are 50% off, according to the store itself) and on top of that there’s also an option to buy the premium currency, which is used for these extra three slots on the lower right hand side…

For anywhere from five bucks to a hundred dollars.

review_title: Greedy, Unfair, and Punishing Loyal Mobile Players
review_text:
Desktop: $19.99 for everything.
Mobile: $6.99 for the game, $14.99 for towers, $19.99 for heroes. Already absurd.

Updates? Free on desktop, but on iOS it’s $6.99 per hero or tower. Now there are three new towers at $5 each, or a $20 bundle — meaning because I supported the game early, I need to spend another $30 just to stay “complete.”

Every time desktop gets free heroes and towers, loyal mobile players are forced to pay another ~$10 just to see the same content. That’s not monetization — that’s punishment.

review_title: The Tyranny of the Evil Eye: A Cancer on Fair Play!
review_text:
The "Evil Eye" direct damage mechanic is an absolute abomination! It is a blight upon the very soul of this game! To call it "difficult" is a lie; it is nothing more than a lazy, incompetent, and utterly disgraceful cheat!
How dare the developers spit in the face of strategy like this?! This mechanic is a direct insult to every player who has ever spent hours refining their deck and mastering their tactics! What is the point of building a defense?! What is the point of managing the board?! The "Evil Eye" ignores it all! It bypasses every rule of fairness with a disgusting, brute-force laziness that makes me sick!
This is not game design; this is a crime against balance! It is a broken, ungodly joke that rewards bad gameplay and punishes skill! It turns a calculated battle into a mindless numbers game! Why should we tolerate a mechanic that acts like a loaded gun pointed at our heads?! It creates a scenario of inevitable loss based on nothing but raw, unfair statistics!
Enough is enough! There is zero honor in this mechanic! It is a coward’s tool! It must be neutered! It must be destroyed! To allow this monstrosity to exist is to admit that you do not care about your players! Remove this plague immediately or watch your game die a well-deserved death! Shame on you!

BUY THIS GAME. If you don’t, you are missing out.

A significant amount of thought, effort, and love clearly went into this game, and it shows in every aspect.

The puzzle design is rock-solid. I completed every puzzle and every solution made sense and felt like a clear result of the clues I was given.

The plant identification is varied and creative, and never feels formulaic — you never know exactly what clue will lead you to identification so identification remains interesting throughout the game.

The single thing I found myself disliking (and the only reason I’m not playing through a second time) was the lack of quick access to the full width of my plant window — simply keeping your identified and unidentified plants separate becomes slightly tedious when you have enough of both it takes more than a second or two to scroll to a new spot; some kind of “overall” view where you could see the whole window at once would help tremendously.

However, that’s the ONLY gripe I had after playing for like 5 hours over multiple sessions and identifying every single plant in the game. Even with that flaw, this game is still 5/5. Brilliantly executed and well worth the money. BUY IT.

review_title: Root, a complex political war game with a cute veneer, made accessible by this digital adaptation.
review_text:
The first thing I noticed about Root was its art: cute anthropomorphic animals in medieval set dressing. Diving further, each group of animals represents a political force or faction in war for the woodland at large. These archetypes are split into two major categories, militants and insurgents. They play differently as their names suggest, militants exert force and generally have a larger presence in the woodland expanding from clearing to clearing, leaving a small garrison behind as their frontlines expand with the bulk of their forces. Insurgents on the other hand can similarly spread albeit without the military might to back that presence, instead their deployments represent a softer form of power that harbors the potential for great violence or exploitation if left unchecked.
Each faction, both militants and insurgents, play differently. This expansive asymmetry and the many different combinations of the factions means no two games truly play the same. There is also a deck of cards with different suits that represent the varied denizens of the woodland, each faction can leverage these cards in their own way to accomplish their goals to end the war in their favor, alongside the universal options that each card offers. There’s more to consider with expansions introducing hirelings (minor versions of each faction that are mutually exclusive with their counterparts), and landmarks (special buildings that add flavor and a new mechanic to a clearing). There’s a lot to this game, I would suggest playing each faction at least once to get a sense of how each can influence the state of the game and its outcome. Also, I hate the vagabond, which is just a comment on my own preference when playing the game.

I’ve been looking for a game that I can play anywhere, without needing internet, WiFi, or data, and that isn’t a MMOPVP city builder/tower defense headache. 

Stumbled upon Subnautica, and it delivers everything I was looking for!!! Yes it’s a paid game, but you’re not constantly required to make micro transactions just to survive. One small fee gets you hours and hours of entertainment, without needing WiFi or data. 

You can choose between various game modes, and still unlock the complete story on the easiest mode. The world is beautifully designed, with lots and lots of areas to explore, hazards to avoid, and really cool things to discover. 

I absolutely love that you can customize your vehicles, and really wish there were more options to customize your bases. Some of the cool plants don’t scan and cannot be collected, so cannot be used to decorate. 

Would love an option like Subnautica: Sub Zero where you can fully customize your game modes, but that’s pretty much my only complaint. Oh, and maybe an interactive map so that I know where I’ve been and what I’ve already explored.
