So after several hours of gameplay with the story line and single player I just gave up at trying to win. I bought several of the DLC clans thinking they would provide advantages and Im still getting failures on the easy level. Mostly it's the impossibility of just surviving. Currently unsure of the disconnect or why most seem to think this game is so awesome, ill try and set up some examples.
First and foremost is the food, one second im up at +35 with full complements of crews working fields/fisheries/and hunting-not counting the several buffs from the lore that ive achieved as well as upgraded storage silos and farms etc. then suddenly without providing feasts or trade routes in food im suddenly starving in summer? no maxed population, I havent even met any other clans to fight but suddenly im starving?? no rats, nor anything that has stolen or disrupted my production, I look at the food icon and no idea how my sudden production now is so far bellow my consumption, which then dumps your happiness which means no new villagers, so I cant build and now I just sit back and watch it all spiral out of control..This was the BEST case ive had so far at coming near to a win..
Second example that happens by far more than anything.
Established again with several buffs, trade routes and several incomes of food and resources, no maxed population and maybe 6-8 warriors and the hero..now, I have multiple (say 3-4) healing huts that are upgraded as well as storage silos, and bang mass rats in everything and the advice? build more healers and upgrade the silos..Uh huh except it all spirals out of control as above-again no enemy, not even an issue with wolves or the Drauhgr. Last example that killed my motivation to play further: Trying the falcon clan after trying the kraken, and bear clan. I picked the falcon because several of the looting advantages looked to hopefully offset the bewildering mass losses of resources.. Again, somewhat established, no enemy encountered, several lore masters on the stones and several buffs-suddenly I can 't feed myself again with a bare minimum of people and with 2 fertile farms, 2 fisheries, one hunters hut, and several looted caches/ships/ruins, and im back to square one ON THE EASY LEVEL..So at this point im done, yup money is gone and its no longer worth dumping time into this.
Now that being said.
The game has several features that seem like decent points:
-myriad of clans with different advantages and disadvantages, I  mean ALLOT of different qualities-one of the major hooking points for me.
-a storyline that mirrors several other past games,survive, build, outlast/build/produce the enemy
-Custom game mode (tried it, still no joy) that allows you to customize the victory scenarios etc.
-Several types of units, that are tailored to each clan, I liked this (or so I thought) because I felt like I could choose my advantages.

-No real crashes or bugs I can attest to that seemed common on past reviews.

-while the controls were somewhat straight forward the game did not have a definite tutorial for game play, once I got around that it was fine.

Ok some points I did not like, ill start from the first play

No tutorial-first info blurb on the screen?select the build icon-uuuh what? ok several different things on the screen, finally I chose the hammer looking thing however I had no idea what the screen information was, I had to tap and play around with it.. so in essence while it would say some hints on the screen, the info wasnt what I needed.

no pause button, i mean no pause button so you can take stock in what is happening, so its all real time, pause it and you go to another screen, unhelpful.

stats for a clan that meant nothing to me, 3 stars for learning how to use the unit? and support? support for what?? no idea-no tutorial to explain it and frankly im not looking to waste days of my life trying to intuit the meaning

complexity of the controls (select/deselect etc.) and the inability to select units with a drag window or something, I dont want my entire army running all over the map, i understood the concept of battle groups but the ability to create them was not very well thought out

imbalance of resources vs supply/unit production..to construct a woodcutters hut, 50 ish wood and the amount it produces is low, same for nearly each resource building vs allowed gains, ya you can add workers to increase production but its still low.

happiness is a joke, I had breweries, lore units, buffs etc. and I could never get it above 6-8 and then it would crash again within a few minutes of gameplay..click on the face and it almost always said -xx population?? seriously, im spread out over half the map and theyre saying its over crowded?? no matter if I had upgraded houses or un maxed populations, still sucked-no matter how many buffs/happiness structures/people/resources I dumped into it, guaranteed negatives with double digits within a game, nearly always due to a starvation issue.. At first I thought it was the winter time but after some monitoring it just didnt make any sense..healers? nope. Trade? nope, better houses? oh after dumping all my stone/workers/wood into upgrades on 4 houses it raised it ONE point..

building an army..K one training camp gives you TWO units, ok sure some buffs increase that, but even then it might give you two more, so now I need to build more camps, and then build different camps to build different units..the amount of resources you dump into them is ridiculous..

Mining-everything in the upgrades REQUIRES STONE, guess what? no mines with stone in your area?? OH WELL S.T.B.Y.! there are metal mines and stone quarries, and oh ya! they dont last for more than 15-20 stone, couple that with it costs 6-10 stone to upgrade one building? ha good luck.

There are a few more points, but since it wont let me write further ill stop. In short not worth my time trying to figure this out despite all the placations the devs will probably drop on this.

review_title: Overpriced for about 40% of the computer game content
review_text:
I’ve watched playthroughs of the computer game and was really excited to play it on my iPad. I am very disappointed. It costs more money to unlock the basic play modes, like campaign. I’ve played through the campaign 3.5 times now, to see if I was missing anything, but no.

About 99% of the time, the neighbors all use the EXACT SAME generic scripts for each interaction. There aren’t any funny excuses for the appearance of obvious doppelgangers. The checklist is only useful for asking for the ID card or entry request, if a neighbor forgot to provide one. You don’t have the option to simply deny entry; you can only let them in or have them killed. The gameplay is GRINDINGLY slow: everything plays so slowly, such as dialogue text and the phone ringing, which you are only allowed to skip entirely but no simply speeding it up. I found myself eventually skipping nearly all dialogue, as soon as I saw that it was just the generic script AGAIN and AGAIN. Many doppelgangers have literally no noticeable differences to the original so the only was to find out is calling the apartment, which makes it so easy that it’s boring. There are no story endings for the campaign mode: at the end of the week, there is zero payoff or reward. For being so prominent in gameplay, the ID numbers and logos do nothing; I have NEVER seen them be anything but correct. On top of all of this, the game is inexcusably glitchy and poorly programmed, especially for a game that costs money.

If you haven’t bought this version yet, don’t bother. It’s like the “baby’s first game” version of the computer version. I’d like it passably if it was a free game but these game devs shouldn’t be charging for this very shaved-down, VERY, VERY BORING excuse for “That’s Not My Neighbor.”

I am super happy with the game as a long time original player but ball is getting stuck on the corner of the coffee building to the point it’s making it hard to complete the next level.

To preface, I’ve put many hours into the original flick home run, and that’s for a reason— the game feels good to play. All of the following points come from a point of love for the original, as I can easily see this becoming an incredible game, but it needs some tweaks (in my opinion). 

This version completely changes the physics system, it now sees almost impossible not to hit a home run. The length your ball reaches is based almost entirely on angle now, rather than speed of the hit or placement on the ball. The hits feel less satisfying and the ball just doesn’t go very far. Also, the vibration is sorely missed. The game generally feels floatier, and less tight in its core mechanic of hitting the ball. 

The health system seems completely broken— I’ve hit balls out of the park just to end up with less health than before the pitch. The amount of points received isn’t locked in when the ball hits the ground, and you can easily lose dozens of points as the ball rolls backwards after a home run. It almost feels random how much health is expended vs earned on each pitch, which just doesn’t feel great.

Leveling up just takes far too long. After clearing 12 stages, I’m just level 4. The balance feels incredibly off, as I only have 6 build points and the second bat. It was maxed out the second I unlocked it, as there’s simply not enough stuff to spend money on with such a low rate of earning levels.  

My last qualm would be with the descriptions of the buildings. They just aren’t clear enough for me to be sure how best to use them. I don’t know if this is an English specific problem, but it’s quite confusing. 

This game has so much potential, even more so than the first game. To the devs, I really hope you guys (or guy idk) can push a few updates in the future to get this game up to the standard of the original, and even beyond. I really appreciate the addition of a progression system for both the bat and constructions out of the stadium, it’s an incredible idea to allow the player to have more ways to progress and create custom “builds” based on the obstacles they place. The first game is an all time classic, and this sequel has the opportunity to build on that, and just be a fun game to play. I would pay a few bucks for this game if it came out in an ad free, completed state like the first one. I think some other people might agree with me based on the success of the original. 

For now I can’t really give it more than a 2.5/5, but I know with just a few updates and fixes it can be a clean 5/5. 

If the dev is reading this, I hope you don’t take anything personally, I really want to see this game achieve greatness. Huge fan.
